claim: §4.11 *The clock* (1) (base l. 8453–8454) defines the document's current week as "the week of the last folded event that carries one" (also §2.9's `EpochRecord` comment, l. 3140, and J-A67.45's index row, l. 22742). R5-03's (4) (l. 8475–8487) and V08 §3.6 (6) (l. 1944–1947) fold a late change "after the last epoch at `W₀` + 1 where `W₁` is after `W₀`, else at `W₀`" and claim that therefore "the document's current week never falls back". That holds only against `W₀`. Between epochs, an absorb with no year end, crossing or calamity folds its element events standalone at their weeks after `W₀` (V08 §3.6 (3), (6)), the usual weekly sync. So after an absorb that folds a Works-beginning change at `W₀` + 3, the next absorb's late change is appended at `W₀` + 1, and by (1) the current week falls back to `W₀` + 1. The drawn present (J-A67.45; *Works* (9)) and every export then show that Works before its start: the house staked a sync ago vanishes. A clock turned back, or a change dated in (`W₀`, current week), does the same. Two builders differ: one derives (1) literally, the other keeps "never falls back". T-V8-49 (g)'s bar ("current week after the absorb not before `W₀`", V08 l. 3311) and T76-1's ("never before it", base l. 18245–18247) pass the regression.
required_change: 1. §4.11 *The clock* (1): "The document's current week is derived — the week of the last folded event that carries one — never a stored counter (§2.9)" → "The document's current week is derived — the greatest week the folded events carry, so an event folded after one of a later week (a late change at `W₀` + 1 or `W₀`, (4); a dossier change dated before an event an earlier absorb folded) never moves it back — never a stored counter (§2.9)". 2. Ends: (model) §2.9's `EpochRecord` comment "the week of the last folded event that carries one" → "the greatest week the folded events carry"; (scope) J-A67.45's index row "(the last folded event's)" → "(the greatest folded week, §4.11 *The clock* (1))"; (V08) T-V8-49 (g), after "the document's current week after the absorb not before `W₀`", adds "; and on a copy, an absorb past `W₀` with no year end, crossing or calamity folding a standalone change at `W₀` + 3 that begins a Works, then an absorb carrying a non-calamity change dated at or before `W₀` — folded at `W₀` + 1, the document's current week still `W₀` + 3 and that Works drawn at its stage there"; (scope) T76-1's late non-calamity clause "the document's current week never before it" → "the document's current week never before it nor before the week of any event an earlier absorb folded". (The adjudicator may instead keep (1) and fold every newly carried change dated before the current week at that week, its tick in its receipt; the bars above then read the same.)

claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised). A primary that S5b spawns, crossing its own stage's boundary on its own viaduct, leaves the stage one gate short of N_k. §4.4 S5b (base l.5907-5918) opens 'The stage's primaries match its gates: N_k = the gate law'. It counts the existing arterials' crossings c 'on ground part 0 (a crossing on a raised deck no gate, S5a Trace (2))'. When N_k > c it spawns N_k - c radials, 'routes each with the incremental S4 router ... and may raise a viaduct by §4.3's rules. The crossings become stage k's main gates.' §4.3 The slot places 'a viaduct ... each later stage's S5b through this router'. S5a Trace (2) pins no gate where 'an arterial crossing the boundary on a raised deck' meets it (l.5856-5857). §2.7's support step (6) (d) makes the stage's ring a stretch laid after that viaduct: 'it takes no crossing station and makes no gate on the deck'. So when a spawned radial raises its viaduct across the valley at its own boundary, the stage gets N_k - 1 gates, and 'primaries match its gates' and §4.8's 'Gates - exactly N, by construction' (l.7655) fail. S5b spawns once and never recounts its own primaries, and no rung or report covers the shortfall. The case is a tested path: T110-2 (2) runs 'a stage-2 S5b viaduct crossed by stage 2's own moated ring' (l.18485-18486), and stage 2's S5b viaducts are its spawned primaries. Its bar checks the ring beneath the deck but no gate count. S5b's own test ('each epoch stage whose N_k exceeds its crossings adds >= 1 primary') passes with the shortfall, and §5.3's counts pass too ('so counted'). So one builder ships N_k - 1 gates, while another spawns a replacement or keeps the viaduct off the boundary. This is new with R5-02: under R4-09 the crossing was a raised gate.
required_change: §4.4 S5b, after 'and may raise a viaduct by §4.3's rules.', add: 'Its own primaries' crossings are counted as c is, on ground part 0: for each spawned primary whose course crosses the boundary on a raised deck, ramp or stair (its viaduct's, which the trace runs on beneath; S5a Trace (2); §2.7's support step (6) (d)), S5b spawns one more by the same nested picks in the same batch, until the stage's crossings on ground part 0 reach N_k or no approachable gap remains - the shortfall then raised and reported as a request below the law is.' S5b's Test adds 'a stage whose spawned primary is raised across its own boundary still has N_k gates on ground part 0'. §4.8 Gates: 'each outer enceinte's gates are its S5b primaries' crossings' -> 'each outer enceinte's gates are its S5b primaries' crossings on ground part 0 (§4.4 S5b)'. End at scope: §13.2 T110-2 (2), after 'a stage-2 S5b viaduct crossed by stage 2's own moated ring', add '- stage 2's gates N_k, each on ground part 0, the viaduct's deck crossing none and one more primary spawned for it'.

claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x C-raised-edit x C-raised-history). A raised gate whose deck is gone. §4.8 Gates (base l.7655-7673) makes a raised gate a main gate of the ring: 'a gate whose tower carries the deck, its portal on the raised part only'. §5.3's gate row checks at S7's stage end 'every gate joined to the network and the plaza' and counts roads leaving a stage at its raised gates (l.9257). The deck can go in three ways: a hand delete of the viaduct (§7.1 Delete; V06 §3.19.3); V06 §3.19.2's lapse and strike, which fall a generated viaduct's spans by stretch; and a landfall, which ruins the spans beside a station (T114-3's landfall clause). The stretch's fate is stated: held while the deck stands, then an ordinary run 'from the first epoch after the raised way is removed or the spans on both sides of the station have fallen' (§2.7's support step (3)). The gate's fate is not. §4.8 does not say whether the Gate stays in Enceinte.gates with a portal onto a deck that no longer exists, nor what becomes of its tower. V06 §3.19.3 (6)'s delete fates list only the arch vaults, 'the route's standing course' and the aqueduct's terminal. One builder keeps a gate joined to nothing, failing §5.3's check or counting a road that is gone. Another drops the gate and its tower, leaving a held stretch with no tower. A third turns it into a ground gate. The path is normal: T114-3 already runs 'a neglected, poor CITY ring over 20 epochs with ... a viaduct on a raised gate'. Two builders build different walls.

claim: §4.11's `wallToWay` (l. 8214–8221) retypes the wall chain as the ring road's spine "on the same edges", excepting only "the stretch held under a raised way's crossing station while its deck stands …, which stays as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, the new ring road taking no junction with the raised way" (VDC4-05's text, this round). Two meetings with a standing raised way have no outcome for the road: (1) that kept stretch stands on the old wall's line, so the road's spine on the same edges runs into the free-standing gate tower or the curtain under the arch (a raised gate's portal is on the raised part only, §4.8 l. 7672–7673); (2) since R5-02 a wall stretch laid after a raised way runs on beneath its deck with each support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span in its band taken into its line and no crossing station (§2.7 (6) (d)), so the save clause does not reach it and the road's spine passes through those parts — a support standing in a road, or a road through an arch vault's chamber (II.7.6). §2.7 (6) (a) makes every part-0 way laid after a raised way cross its under-deck strip only by §4.3's crossing rule, else end at the strip, but `wallToWay` neither cites nor applies it, nor does V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s bullet ("leave standing every raised way that crosses the old line; the new ring road takes no junction with it"). The path is an ordinary one at growing CITY and METROPOLIS epochs (a superseded ring's `road` end, V06 §3.7.2 (3); case (1) is H-AQUA's own CITY ring under its founded aqueduct, run by T-V6-47; case (2) T110-2's lead fixture once its stage-2 ring is superseded). Two builders: the road through the supports or the kept stretch, or the road re-routed or ended at the strip. Untested: T-V6-47's `wallToWay` clause checks only that the raised way and its station stand.

V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s absorb bullet says only that the new ring road takes no junction with a raised way. So at the pathway's `road` fate (V06 §3.7.2 (3), l. 1486) or a hand `convert` `wallToWay` of a ring laid after a raised way, nothing says how the road passes it. Taken literally, the primary way's spine runs over the support rings and through a `vault` span's chamber, against (6) (a) ('everything laid after the raised way gives way to it') and against T110-2's and T-V6-47's bar '0 way corridors over a support ring, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span'. Builders diverge (through the pier, ended at the strip, bent under a span); no bar runs it.

claim: R5-03 makes a late calamity carried by an absorb whose week is not after the last epoch's **held** "until the first epoch a later absorb folds" (base §4.11 *The clock* (4); V08 §3.6 (3); §7.7's comment "held for the first epoch a later absorb folds"; V08 §2.6's row: read by "the port's next absorb"), and states that it "is never lost … its hazard strikes and its deaths reach the burial need". A **detached what-if copy** (V06 §4.4: `forkAt` at the head, the alternative V06 §2.3 and §3.3 offer for `advance` on a dossier-bound document) keeps the dossier's facts and so the folded binding, `lateCalamities` included, and is advanced by V06's `advance`, but "no later dossier event reaches it". No text carries a held calamity into an epoch not folded by an absorb, so in the copy it never strikes — the outcome R5-03 forbids — and since the list is rewritten only by `dossierFacts` events, which the copy never receives, a builder who does carry it into the copy's first epoch has nothing to clear it and strikes it again at every later epoch. Two builders: one never strikes it (V06 §4.4 and §2.3 as written), one strikes it once or at every epoch ("never lost"). The held state can last most of a year (a later absorb with no year end, crossing or new calamity folds no epoch), so a DM's what-if copy in that time is an ordinary use of the alternative V06 offers. Principle (11): a combination edge (a fork while a calamity is held) with no defined outcome and no test.
